name: iComply — Municipal Ordinance Change Monitor
one_line_value_proposition: Watches municipal ordinance pages, detects changes by content hash and delivers signed webhooks with a diff summary.
buyer_problem: Contractors, short-term-rental operators and compliance teams track local rules that change on scattered municipal websites with no change feed.
solution_summary_public: A Next.js 14 + Prisma + Postgres service with a dashboard, cron-driven scraping (robots.txt honored), per-target intervals, baseline-then-diff detection, retrying signed webhooks and failure handling that parks failing targets.
differentiators_public: SSRF guard resolved at connect time (DNS-rebinding safe), redirect re-validation and response size cap.
Webhook signatures with timestamp skew rejection; secrets encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.
robots.txt honored by default; failing targets are parked and reported.
verified_capabilities: Vitest suite: 30 tests passed, 1 skipped (integration needs Postgres), 2026-10-15; GitHub Actions workflow 'icomply' succeeded on main at 934c993.
Dashboard with fail-closed basic auth in production; health endpoint; cron endpoint with bearer secret.
Includes a separate municipal-compliance pipeline (scrape, diff, LLM analysis, alerts) in the same repository.
unverified_claims: Production deployment and real-world scraping coverage across municipalities.
Accuracy of the LLM analysis in the municipal-compliance pipeline.
Integration test against a live Postgres in this review.

public.headline: Know when a city ordinance page changes — and get a signed webhook, not a surprise.
public.subheadline: iComply scrapes configured municipal pages on a schedule, records baselines, detects changes with SHA-256 hashing and notifies your systems through HMAC-signed webhooks.
public.cost_of_inaction: Missing a local rule change can mean non-compliant operations. Qualitative statement; no market statistic is cited.
public_limitations: Scraping legality and terms vary by municipality; the operator must respect each site's terms.
Not legal advice; the software detects changes, it does not interpret law.
No customers, revenue or traction verified.
architecture_public: Scheduler/cron → scraper (Cheerio, SSRF-guarded) → content hash compare → change record + diff summary → signed webhook delivery with retries → Postgres via Prisma.
public.risk_summary: Scraping/terms exposure per jurisdiction; unverified production behavior; overlapping earlier variants must be excluded or disclosed; ownership review pending.
